meta.title: Type error after undo
meta.fix_ref: edaeab2bc (Mutate sourceFile imports list whenever it changes, #8986), 2024-09-13; git tag --contains: first in 1.1.381
meta.build_notes: npm pyright@1.1.380 (2024-09-10) and pyright@1.1.381 (2024-09-17). The reporter's last comment says 1.1.380 fixed his case (that was the related #8919); the fix of this mechanism (edaeab2bc) is first in 1.1.381, and the spike reproduced the bug on 1.1.380 and not on 1.1.381.
meta.notes: Converted from the validated state-bug spike (scripts/lsp_repro/cases/pyright_8946.py, 'plain' variant: the verbatim code only; the spike's sentinel line is not part of the issue and is not used). Mechanism from the fix commit: when the new import list is a subset of the old one the sourceFile's import list is not mutated, so restoring the import does not re-register the file in the stub's importedBy list and the stub is collected as unneeded; its symbols stop resolving. Headlessly the restored Pool resolves to Unknown (fewer errors rather than more, the opposite sign of the issue's wording); settling between the delete and the undo is what lets the collection run.

settings_note: The issue names no settings (a stand-alone file); the session defaults (basic type checking, open files only) apply.

repro.steps: Open main.py and let the server analyze it. Remove the line 'from multiprocessing import Pool' (errors appear), then undo the delete, as an editor does, by re-inserting the same line; the server settles after each step. Reported: after the undo, errors stay and Pool is not a recognized type. Probe (R1): hover and definition at the restored Pool use in 'with Pool(workers)' and the diagnostics of main.py must equal those of a fresh session on the same (original) text.
